title: Sewer lateral repair in Lawrence, Indiana | Indy Sewer Resource

claims.note: Ordinance 5-1-1-2(A)(11): building sewer runs from the building drain to the public sewer and includes the right-of-way portion.
Ordinance 5-1-2-7, restated to homeowners by the utility in 2023 and again in August 2024.
Reconciliation of three consistent sources; labeled as reasoning on the page. The tap/wye at the main is explicitly NOT established.
Utility newsletter guidance, including that the City does not reimburse contractor costs when the fault is in the public main.

Method mechanics are now cited to engineering specifications issued by a government body (HRPDC Sections 824 and 815), plus Lawrence policy for the sectional-liner and replacement cases. The page labels them as general descriptions, not Lawrence requirements, and makes no suitability, lifespan, price, or success-rate claim.

The current City form covers Repair/Modification Work and Replace/Relocate, requires a plat drawing with materials, a Lawrence contractor registration number, and an emergency application by the next business day. It states no fee and no submission address; both remain unestablished.
The after-hours number published in August 2024 is printed with its date, and the page tells readers to check the City site for the current number.
The utility own statement about older clay laterals. No prevalence figure appears anywhere on the page, because none exists in the evidence.
The utility reported an increase in laterals damaged by fiber and 5G contractors. No counts, and no entitlement, are implied.
Public-system projects with the City own documented methods and quantities. The page states explicitly that these do not establish suitability or cost for any private lateral.
Presented as a question to ask a contractor, not as a rule binding a private repair; the 24-48 hour notice and the 8-hour limit bind the City contractor on its own project.

That CCTV identifies defect type, condition, position along the line, and extent, while surface location and burial depth generally need separate locating or further investigation, is our reading of how the cited documents use camera work. It is worded cautiously on the page and is a candidate for expert-review correction.
The utility cites ordinance 5-1-2-2; that ordinance text was not independently re-read, and the page says so.
